title: Scalper Discipline
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/0/body: A **daily loss limit** is an amount you set in advance. If today's loss reaches it, **you stop trading for the rest of the day**. For example, 2% of the account, or 3 losses in a row.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/1/body: A scalper makes **dozens of decisions** in a few hours. After a few losses in a row, your mind starts chasing a **quick comeback**, and decision quality drops. A daily limit stops **one bad day** from turning into a **disastrous loss**.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/1/tip: Write your limit down before the day starts. The heat of the moment is no time to decide.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/2/prompt: Your account is $8,000 and your daily loss limit is 1.5% of the account. What's the most you can lose today?
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/2/explanati: 8,000 × 0.015 = $120. Once today's loss hits $120, your trading day is over.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/3/statement: Once you hit your daily loss limit, the right move is to stop trading for the rest of the day, even if you see a good setup.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/3/explanati: A limit you break for a “good” setup isn't a limit. The rule has to stop you exactly when the urge to keep going is strongest. Tomorrow's setups will still be there.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/4/prompt: Your daily loss limit is $150 and you risk $50 per trade. You've lost $60 and $50 so far and just spotted a new setup. What do you do?
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/4/options/0: Skip it; only $40 is left before the limit
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/4/options/1: Take it; I haven't hit the limit yet
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/4/options/2: Go in with double size to win it back
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/4/explanati: 150 − 110 = $40 of room left, but a full loss on the next trade is $50, which breaks the limit. Either the risk drops below $40 or the day ends. Many scalpers call it quits right here.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/5/body: On top of a dollar limit, many scalpers also have a **losing streak rule**: for example, after **3 losses in a row**, take at least a 30-minute break or end the day. This rule stops **revenge trading**.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/6/sentence: Set your daily loss limit ___ trading starts, and when you hit it, close the ___.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/6/explanati: Risk decisions should be made with a calm mind, before the market opens. Hitting the limit means stepping out of the market completely for today.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/7/prompt: Put a scalper's daily risk management in order.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/7/items/0: Write down your daily loss limit
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/7/items/1: Set your risk per trade from that limit
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/7/items/2: After each trade, add up today's losses
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/7/items/3: When you hit the limit, end the day
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/7/explanati: Limit first, then risk per trade (say a quarter of the limit). During the day you keep a running tally of losses, and when you hit the limit, you stop, no bargaining.
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/8/pairs/0/m: The most you're allowed to lose in a day
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/8/pairs/2/m: A rushed entry to win back a loss
lessons/scalping-u3-l1/steps/8/pairs/3/m: What you lose if your stop loss is hit
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/0/body: **Overtrading** means trading without a real setup: out of **boredom**, excitement or to win back a loss. It costs a scalper even more, because **every extra trade also pays spread and commission**.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/1/prompt: You take 40 trades a day with 1 lot on EUR/USD, and each trade costs 1 pip. What do the trading costs alone come to in one day?
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/1/explanati: 40 × 1 pip × $10 = $400, just for getting in and out. A trade with no setup adds this cost for no reason.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/2/statement: The more scalps you take in a day, the more profit you're guaranteed to make.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/2/explanati: Only trades with positive expectancy build profit. A trade without a setup just adds costs and losses.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/3/body: Focus is limited. After a few hours of staring at a 1-minute chart, your **decision speed and quality** drop. Many scalpers only trade a **short 2- to 3-hour session** during volatile hours and put a **cap** on their number of trades.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/4/prompt: It's 19:00 London time and you've been at the chart for 5 hours. What does the market look like now, and what's the best move?
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/4/options/0: Volatility and volume have dropped; end the session
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/4/options/1: The market is calm; increase your size
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/4/options/2: A strong trend has started; trade more
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/4/explanati: Candles have shrunk and volume keeps falling. Price movement barely covers costs anymore. Add 5 hours of fatigue, and it's the worst possible combo for scalping.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/5/prompt: Which one is a sign of overtrading?
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/5/options/0: Entering just because you haven't traded in a few minutes
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/5/options/1: Waiting until every setup condition is met
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/5/options/2: Ending the session at the planned time
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/5/options/3: Passing on a setup that's missing a condition
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/5/explanati: Boredom isn't a reason to enter. The other options are exactly the discipline that prevents overtrading.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/6/pairs/0/m: Trading beyond your plan, without setups
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/6/pairs/1/m: Fear of missing out on a move
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/6/pairs/2/m: Worse decisions after hours of trading
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/6/pairs/3/m: Max trades allowed in one session
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/7/sentence: To avoid overtrading, cap the ___ of daily trades and only enter when the ___ is complete.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/7/explanati: A trade cap cuts out the extra trades, and the “complete setups only” rule keeps the quality of the rest high.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/8/prompt: Put a healthy scalping session in order.
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/8/items/0: Set your session time and trade cap
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/8/items/2: Take a break after 2 losses in a row
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/8/items/3: Close the session at the set time
lessons/scalping-u3-l2/steps/8/explanati: The rules are written before the session, trades happen only at the right time, breaks stop losing streaks, and the session ends by the clock, not by how you feel.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/0/body: **Win rate** alone tells you nothing. You also need your **average win** and **average loss**. **Expectancy** combines them: how much each trade makes or loses on average, **after costs**.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/1/prompt: Win rate is 50%, the average win is 6 pips and the average loss is 4 pips (all after costs). What's the expectancy per trade?
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/1/explanati: 0.5 × 6 − 0.5 × 4 = 3 − 2 = +1 pip. So over the long run, each trade makes 1 pip net on average.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/2/statement: A 70% win rate on its own means the strategy is profitable.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/2/explanati: If the average loss is 3 times the average win: 0.7 × 1 − 0.3 × 3 = −0.2. So even with a 70% win rate, you lose money overall.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/3/body: Log every trade in a **journal**: time, setup, entry and exit, costs and your state of mind. **Profit factor** = total wins ÷ total losses; above 1 means profitable. Before you judge anything, collect a **big enough sample** (say 50 to 100 trades).
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/4/prompt: This month, total wins were $900 and total losses were $600. What's the profit factor?
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/4/explanati: 900 ÷ 600 = 1.5, so you make $1.50 for every $1 you lose. 0.67 is the ratio flipped upside down.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/5/explanati: The winners' share minus the losers' share. If the result is positive, the strategy has an edge over the long run.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/6/prompt: Put your weekly performance review in order.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/6/items/0: Pull all of the week's trades from your journal
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/6/items/1: Subtract costs and work out the net result
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/6/items/2: Break the results down by setup and time
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/6/items/3: Cut or fix the worst setup or time slot
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/6/explanati: Without complete, net data, any analysis is misleading. Breaking it down by setup and time shows exactly where your profits and losses come from.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/7/prompt: Your journal of the last 80 trades shows the EMA setup during the London–New York overlap has +0.8 pips expectancy, but trades after 18:00 London time have −0.5 pips. What's the most sensible decision?
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/7/options/0: Drop the trades after 18:00 and focus on the overlap
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/7/options/1: Trade bigger after 18:00 to win back the losses
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/7/options/2: Ditch the EMA setup entirely since some trades lost
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/7/options/3: Stop journaling because the numbers are confusing
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/7/explanati: The data says your edge lives in the overlap and disappears after 18:00 (probably from lower volatility and fatigue). Cutting the losing part without touching the winning part is the smartest fix.
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/8/pairs/2/m: Total wins divided by total losses
lessons/scalping-u3-l3/steps/8/pairs/3/m: The account's drop from its peak
